summary.headline: M&B Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% to INR291 crores; order book INR1,053 crores, but management withholds FY27 margin guidance for one more quarter.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew about 22.5% YoY to INR291 crores, with PAT up 22% to INR22 crores. Operating EBITDA was INR33 crores (11.4% margin) against reported EBITDA of INR36 crores. Order on hand stood at INR1,053 crores (up about 25% YoY), though Q1 order inflow of about INR260 crores was softer, which management attributed to large inquiries slipping into Q2. Freight costs (US-bound, roughly 2x to 2.5x since March) and steel prices (up 10-12%) are compressing margins, so management reiterated the 25%+ FY27 revenue growth target but declined to give a margin guide until Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~1,400 MT vs ~INR3 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,053 crores (Phenix INR837 crores, Proflex INR216 crores)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.19 lakh YoY; vs INR1.38 lakh QoQ

segments.name: Phenix (PEB and heavy structural steel)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR214 crores, up 22% YoY; order book INR837 crores including export orders of INR278 crores to be executed mostly in FY27, about 28% dispatched to date. Sanand running at 75-80% utilisation.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported steel roofing)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR77 crores, up 25% YoY; order book INR216 crores. Installed capacity raised to 21 lakh sq m per annum after commissioning two mobile manufacturing units.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue INR28 crores (about 1,400 MT); management guides about 15% sustainable export EBITDA at current freight, 16-18% in normal freight, versus about 11% domestic. More than 8,000 MT expected in the remaining three quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of over 25% in FY27, implying about INR1,600 crores top line.
No specific FY27 margin guidance; management targets improvement over the current 11-11.5% operating EBITDA margin but will guide at Q2 results (next quarter).
Sanand 20,000 TPA brownfield expansion (PEB capacity 72,000 to 92,000 TPA) commissioning in October 2026, benefits in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to start this fiscal, completion Q3 FY28; total capacity about 1,54,000-1,55,000 TPA.
Over 20% CAGR over the next three to four years in the medium-term plan, with progressive profitability improvement.
Targeted PEB volume of 85,000-90,000 MT in FY27 versus 72,000 MT last year.
capex_capacity: Sanand PEB brownfield: +20,000 TPA, commissioning October 2026; PEB capacity to 92,000 TPA.

INR30 crores fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand, adding 10,000 tons to existing 12,000 tons; operational by Q1 FY28. Board approved an additional heavy structural expansion at Sanand.

Cheyyar (South India) is AISC certified, enabling exports to US West Coast via Pacific route from next fiscal; brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to complete in Q3 FY28; utilisation targeted at about 60% this fiscal.
Proflex installed capacity 21 lakh sq m per annum after two mobile manufacturing units.
2.5 MW ground-mounted captive solar plant in Gujarat under development.
Third plant site under evaluation in North India; to be announced once finalised.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow about INR260 crores; management says large inquiries have rubber-banded into Q2. Management cites an INR4,000 crore Phenix inquiry pipeline and about INR200 crores in Proflex.
Hit rate of 12-15% over the last five years, with a stated policy of protecting margins over chasing volume; peers reportedly near 20%.
Freight costs to US roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container); US Section 232 duty cut from 50% to 25%; US steel up about 10-12% since March; domestic freight up 2-5%.
Roughly 80-85% of raw material is booked at order booking; 15-20% is left open to price variation. Domestic PEB margins down 1-2% due to inflation.
Management says domestic market share is about 10-12%, targeting 15% over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order inflow weak at about INR260 crores versus the INR100 crore/month run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said inflow was up 25% YoY; large inquiries took longer on design freeze and have rubber-banded into Q2. Management says the run rate of about INR100 crores of PEB per month is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export margin and how much does freight affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Majmudar said the balance INR278 crores export order book yields about 15% EBITDA at peak freight, 16-17% in a better scenario; domestic is about 11%, so the gap has narrowed to about 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Phenix realisation per MT fall QoQ to INR1.25 lakh from INR1.38 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah attributed it to export mix (under 10%) and project-specific bought-out items, not price cuts; management expects full-year comparability.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic PEB realisation flat despite higher steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said domestic tonnage rose about 6.6% and revenue 7.6%; raw material cost was about 0.5% lower YoY and product mix (primary vs sheeting) drove the gap. Higher steel costs will show in orders booked at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Cheyyar capacity come in Q1/Q2 FY28 or Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said the Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion comes in Q3 FY28, giving two effective quarters in FY28; Sanand's additional capacity arrives in Q3-Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a specific range, saying it will give guidance after one more quarter; the target is to improve over the current 11-11.5% operating margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the win rate on bids?
qa_highlights.answer: Chirag Patel said the win rate is 10-12%, up to 12-15% depending on order; large customers take longer to finalise engineering.

risks_watch: FY27 margin guidance deferred to Q2 results; management says it will give specific guidance only after one more quarter, so the 11-11.5% operating EBITDA base is the only reference point for now.

Freight and US tariff exposure: US-bound freight roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container) with management saying freight is unlikely to be sustainable, yet pass-through is incomplete; export margin guided at about 15% at peak freight vs 16-18% normal.

Order inflow pacing: Q1 inflow about INR260 crores; large inquiries have slipped into Q2. Watch whether the roughly INR100 crore per month run rate is maintained against a INR4,000 crore Phenix pipeline and a 12-15% historical hit rate.

Capacity ramp timing: Sanand 20,000 TPA expansion due October 2026 (benefits Q3-Q4 FY27); Sanand heavy structural line by Q1 FY28; Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion in Q3 FY28. Any slippage would constrain the 25%+ revenue target and the 85,000-90,000 MT PEB volume goal.

Raw material pass-through: about 80-85% of steel is booked at order booking, with domestic PEB margins already down 1-2% from inflation. Management expects higher steel costs to show up in fresh orders, so the lag between price and margin needs tracking.
Export order execution: INR278 crore export order book to be executed over the next three quarters, about 28% dispatched so far; more than 8,000 MT expected in the remaining quarters of FY27.
key_quotes: While our objective is to improve margins on a full year basis, given the continuing uncertainty on the cost front rising from the West Asia crisis, we would prefer to wait for at least one more quarter before providing specific margin guidance for the year.
So, I will not run after orders just to make my hit rate 20% by letting go of my margins.
But at the same time, I am repeating myself that it will not come at the cost of my bottom line or my margin targets, Meaning both have to go hand in hand.
Sanjay Majmudar: Yes, 100%. Sir, we are talking of improving from 11% to 11.5%. There's no question. Blended margin, I am talking, okay?
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on top-line growth (25%+ FY27 guidance, INR4,000 crore pipeline, 60-70% repeat customers) but cautious on margins, declining to give a FY27 margin number until Q2 because of freight and steel cost volatility tied to the West Asia situation. Answers on the hit rate and capacity were firm and strategy-led, while the explanation of Q1 realisation and order inflow was defensive, attributing both to timing, mix and rubber-banded inquiries rather than pricing.
